“... We cannot think of the Lord Christ except as the One who sits at the right hand of the Father; we cannot consider the Lord Christ except as the One who is in Heaven and everywhere: everywhere with His Divinity and in Heaven with His human nature...” (Father Teofil Părăian)
b513c9a461d4:
“All grown-ups were once children, but few of them remember it...” (The Little Prince)

We remember our childhood looking at the Little Prince alongside invented characters (the puppy and the cat) in a charming painting on glass, ordered by one of the first people who appreciated, and still appreciate, our icons.

Happy Children's Day to children big and small!
ec71c6a5bd8b:
A new icon with a special theme, painted in our workshop: the Nativity of the Lord Jesus Christ.
It is inspired by an icon from 1869 (Savu Moga, Arpașu de Sus, which was itself inspired by woodcuts).

About the icon:
The Nativity scene is dominated by Jesus on His swaddling cloth, surrounded by the kneeling Holy Mary, by Joseph and by the other figures named in the painters' manuals: the three Magi, the shepherds, the two animals – the ox and the horse – and the star that guides the Magi and whose rays come down upon the Child Jesus.
At the top, two angels display the text “The Nativity of the Lord Jesus Christ”.

The icon is not available. If you would like an icon on this theme, contact me.

25 April: «The Life-giving Spring»

⊹ A feast on Bright Friday... It is a feast dedicated to the Mother of God, recalling the role of the Virgin Mary in the salvation of mankind.

⊹ A warm feast dedicated to the Mother of God, reminding us of Good Friday, of the tears and pain of the Sorrowful Mother... Then, the Mother of God suffered and wept beside the Saviour's Cross.
Today, the tears of the Mother of God are a Healing Spring of hope and of healing from illness, wounds and suffering.

⊹ The icon we are showing you today is “The Sorrowful Mother of God”, painted in our workshop (model: Savu Moga, Țara Făgărașului, 1877).

c9a3faae13db:
«The Eucharistic Christ» – icon on glass (model: Șcheii Brașovului, early 19th century)

“The power and essence of the Sacrament of the Eucharist in the Orthodox Church lie in the fact that, in the form of the bread and wine consecrated at the Holy Liturgy, the Body and Blood of Jesus Christ are truly given to us.
This sacramental realism is felt and lived by every Orthodox believer who approaches Holy Communion, and it is hard to put into words and even harder to render in any iconographic image.

Yet the Romanian peasant, forced by circumstances, managed to create an icon unique in the world, of theological composition, with a deep and original message, which defends Eucharistic realism without any ambiguity.
This is the icon known as «Jesus Christ – the True Vine», but which should more correctly be called «the Eucharistic Christ», because it is not about the metaphor of the vine but about the Eucharist, in which the Body and Blood of Christ are truly present.

The context in which this icon appeared is not known from historical documents, but it can easily be deduced from the troubled history of Transylvania.
More precisely, the icon was born when, from the 16th century on, Calvinist proselytism appeared in Transylvania, disputing any sacramental realism and claiming that the Holy Sacraments had only a symbolic value.“ (Rev. Assoc. Prof. Dr. Irimie Marga)
